**BWHP142** is the Danish procedure code designating treatment with mirikizumab, a newer interleukin-23 (IL-23) inhibitor [^src1]. It is tracked within the national registry to monitor the clinical administration of [[bmsl|Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] (biological and targeted synthetic drugs) among patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in Denmark [^src1]. 

According to Appendix Table 6 of the 2025 DANIBD report, the clinical adoption of BWHP142 during the specific reporting period from October 1, 2024, to September 30, 2025, was highly restricted [^src1]. Specifically, there were no registered treatments using this code among pediatric patients, and its application among adult patients remained limited [^src1]. 

The documentation of BWHP142 is part of a broader set of technical appendix tables in the DANIBD report that record the use of biological treatments and surgical interventions [^src1]. These tables serve as the evidence base for national quality indicators—specifically indicator 5 for biological treatment—and provide detailed demographic, diagnostic, and treatment data at both the national and hospital levels [^src1]. Ultimately, tracking procedure codes like BWHP142 is central to the registry's role in evaluating treatment variations, surgical practices, and patient access to advanced IBD therapies across the country [^src1].
